response.markdown_report:
At 20% progress, select the **endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff experiment**: its small intervention offers an interpretable next step before adding architecture.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Broad associations displace specific current preferences; terminal prediction may encourage context-specific discrimination. (2) Historical purchases generate redundant suggestions; recent-prefix supervision tests whether historical affinity can become more selective, although recency cannot identify unresolved needs. (3) Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile training margins (−0.1487 and −0.2356), motivating better discrimination. (4) Missing training-allocation counters prevent attributing those failures to branch imbalance; diagnostic terminal coverage cannot recover that information.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) supports masked reconstruction and appended-mask prediction, making strict-prefix supervision compatible with the required family. (2) [MARS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) motivates finer semantic distinctions, but its pretrained text approach does not establish benefits from scratch-trained text features. (3) [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) motivates temporal relations; adapting these to bidirectional attention remains a separate hypothesis.

The framework separates three directions: **target exposure → sampling**, **item specificity → semantic representation**, and **historical relevance → temporal attention**. Keep the other two axes fixed when testing one.

Scores below use O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each cell gives a positive and a limitation.

| Atomic idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-cutoff mixture; BERT4Rec | 2: precise control / established ingredients | 6: guides exposure studies / confounded mediators | 7: targets stale affinity / cannot infer need | 7: targets weak margins / effect unverified | 3: sampler edit / bookkeeping care |
| Joint gated title/description residual; MARS-inspired | 4: constrained adaptation / familiar fusion | 7: shares lexical evidence / weak supervision | 8: finer specifications and moods / text may omit suitability | 6: finer separation / may oversmooth | 6: one network / vocabulary and scoring integration |
| Learned time-gap attention bias; TiSASRec-inspired | 3: family adaptation / established timing | 6: adaptive relevance / sparse timestamps | 7: addresses stale occasions / recent need remains unknown | 5: richer contexts / concentration is not causal evidence | 6: scalar biases / timestamp-interface changes |

**Selected algorithm.** Establish equal, separately normalized reconstruction and terminal losses with uniform nonterminal cutoffs. Then change only conditional nonterminal sampling to 50% uniform and 50% uniform over the latest ten eligible positions. Fix final-event selection at 0.1 when alternatives exist. This explicitly targets broad matches displacing present preferences, stale purchase demand, and weak positive–negative separation.

Measure cutoff allocation and branch losses; select through unchanged macro validation HR@10. Historical scores 0.5825–0.5850 do not establish a controlled improvement. Retain one BERT4Rec checkpoint per category; never combine arms.

idea.description: Test endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff sampling against an established uniform-cutoff control, using one jointly trained BERT4Rec per category and identical separately normalized reconstruction and terminal objectives.
idea.motivation: The intervention targets two reported user failures: broad associations outranking specific present preferences and historical purchases implying continuing demand. Strict-prefix terminal discrimination may help, but cannot identify completed needs or compatibility. Negative lower-tail sampled training margins in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics motivate the experiment without establishing its expected validation benefit.
idea.implementation_notes: Establish the uniform control first; supplied historical scores do not demonstrate that it exists. If the corrected baseline lacks the two-branch objective, creating that control is a separate intervention. Between control and treatment preserve architecture, optimizer, reconstruction corruption, user eligibility, output-head denominator, sampling corrections, checkpoint selection and validation schedule. Use loss=0.5*reconstruction_sum/Nr+0.5*terminal_sum/Nt; require both counts positive. Retain users with at least two training events and document excluded users. Preserve earlier repeated target occurrences in strict-prefix histories; the selected occurrence and all subsequent events must be absent. Reconstruction must retain genuine masked-target supervision without visible shifted labels. Use reserved MASK and maximum nonpadding-index readout with left padding. For n=2 choose the sole eligible endpoint; for n>=3 endpoint probability is 0.1. Recent sampling concerns event positions, not elapsed time. Reconstruction can also supervise the endpoint, so 0.1 is not total endpoint supervision mass. Use matched user batches and cutoff uniforms with separate deterministic data RNG streams derived from seed 42; document changes from baseline RNG draws. Persist measured training branch counts, coefficient masses, target-weighted CE, endpoint exceptions, target-frequency/context-length distributions and timing alongside checkpoints. These measures cannot establish gradient shares. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches per executed epoch, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200 capped at 200. Retain all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], fixed splits, single-GPU execution and trial-local artifacts. All trials and diagnostics consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), family-specific sample_batch and ModelView compatibility, including actual view.model, item_emb, log2feats and predict_score. Restore training counters explicitly; diagnosis-loader coverage cannot replace them. Preserve the embedded predictor writer and appended-mask inference; no architecture change is required. Each category loads exactly one trained checkpoint without averaging or score fusion. Use only permitted histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Evaluate with the pinned host macro validation HR@10. If aligned per-user hits are supplied, report paired gained/lost hits; otherwise do not invent them. Inspect the same twenty training users' full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for specific willingness to choose, redundancy and mood/specification mismatch. Sampled validation gains do not establish those qualitative improvements. Target frequency and context length are potential mediators of the sampling effect, requiring later separate controls.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np

CATEGORIES = ('Movies_and_TV', 'Industrial_and_Scientific',
              'Electronics', 'CDs_and_Vinyl')

def data_rng(category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id):
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence(
        [42, category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id]))

def choose_target(history, u, treatment):
    n = len(history)
    if n < 2:
        raise ValueError('Sample from the shared eligible-user population')
    if n == 2:
        return 1, 'singleton_endpoint_exception'
    if u < 0.1:
        return n - 1, 'endpoint'
    v = (u - 0.1) / 0.9
    m = n - 2
    probabilities = np.full(m, 1.0 / m)
    if treatment:
        k = min(10, m)
        probabilities *= 0.5
        probabilities[-k:] += 0.5 / k
    cdf = probabilities.cumsum()
    cdf[-1] = 1.0
    j = min(int(np.searchsorted(cdf, v, side='right')), m - 1)
    return j + 1, 'nonterminal'

originality.positive: Fixed endpoint probability and separately normalized objectives define a precise, interpretable sampling comparison.
originality.negative: Masked terminal prediction and recency-biased sampling are established ingredients; the contribution is primarily experimental.

future_potential.positive: A feasible early experiment can determine whether target exposure merits more expensive semantic or temporal extensions.
future_potential.negative: Sampling changes context length and item exposure together, and cannot directly infer unresolved demand.

code_difficulty.positive: The treatment changes a sampler while retaining the BERT4Rec architecture and inference computation.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact loss semantics, matched randomness, persistent counters and short-history exceptions require careful integration.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item modeling for sequential recommendation.
Provides the family-compatible foundation for reserved-mask training and terminal-mask inference.
limitations: Does not establish the benefit of the proposed fixed-endpoint recent-cutoff distribution.
Interaction prediction does not directly identify unresolved needs or product suitability.

related_work.title: MARS
contributions: Motivates attribute-aware semantic representations and finer user–item matching.
limitations: Its pretrained-language-model approach does not establish effectiveness of a small text encoder trained from scratch.
Only supplied titles and descriptions are available for a compatible adaptation.

related_work.title: TiSASRec: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models temporal intervals within sequential attention.
Motivates a later jointly trained temporal-bias experiment.
limitations: Its backbone cannot replace the required BERT4Rec family.
Temporal proximity does not establish current demand, and a bidirectional adaptation needs separate evaluation.
